newsitem.title: POLAND: Gdansk refinery to buy oil during 2-month break.
newsitem.headline: Gdansk refinery to buy oil during 2-month break.

text.p: The Gdansk refinery will shutdown for renovation from April 28 to June 22 and will import 500,000 tonnes of refined oil products to maintain its sales, the head of the refinery said.

Wlodzimierz Dyrka told a news conference on Wednesday the firm would not increase its stocks beforehand, because of a strike alert in the company and because high world oil prices made such purchases unprofitable.

Unions in the refinery, Poland's second largest at around 60,000 barrels per day, staged a one-hour warning strike on Wednesday to press for free shares in the firm, wage rises and a shorter working week.
"Considering the strike readiness in the company, the refinery does not intend to build up its reserves because at current prices it would be highly unprofitable," Dyrka said.
Maximum prices of fuel in Poland are set by the finance ministry, which is reluctant to let them rise because of the fear of inflation.
